newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REGGIE WHITE TO FINISH CAREER AS GREEN BAY PACKER.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REGGIE WHITE TO FINISH CAREER AS GREEN BAY PACKER.

text.p: The Green Bay Packers on Thursday announced that they had reached an agreement with defensive end Reggie White that will keep the National Football League's all-time sacks leader on the team for the remainder of his career.
The team did not release the terms of the deal, but the Green Bay Press-Gazette reported that the contract was for $19 million over five years.
White, who will turn 35 next week, was in the final year of a four-year contract he signed as an unrestricted free agent in April, 1993.
"I believe it speaks for itself when the most dominant defensive player of his era elects to finish his career as a Green Bay Packer," general manager Ron Wolf said of White.
"I speak for every member of the Packer organisation when I say we are delighted that Reggie White has decided to end his career wearing the green and gold."
The 6-5 (1.65 m), 300-pound (136 kg) White Thursday was named to an NFL-record 11th straight Pro Bowl.
White, who spent the first eight seasons of his 12-year NFL career with the Eagles, has amassed 162 1/2 sacks in 182 career games with Philadelphia and Green Bay.
He has twice led the league in sacks -- with 21 in 1987 and 18 in 1988.
